transcript:
Header: 2025-04-22 | 16:00 PDT | Duration: 52 min
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Luca (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Product), Jordan (BrightRoute Head of ML), Sofia (Platform), Markus (CTO)
Shared links: Redwood benchmark spreadsheet (drive link), quick console tour recording (rwd.co/console-tour), security one-pager (rwd.co/sec-onepager)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough): walked through model catalog and benchmarks, demoed Optimize recommendations, answered questions about VPC and private deployment. Agreed to send benchmarks + start POC.

[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, uh we're Maya from Redwood. On the call I got Luca our SE and Priya from product for the catalog/Optimize walkthrough. Jordan, do you want to quick intro?

[00:00:16] Jordan: Yeah sure, Jordan Miles, head of ML at BrightRoute. We're building a routing optimization product that uses LLMs for plan explanation and reranking. Main concerns: sub-200ms p95 for short prompts and data privacy.

[00:00:30] Sofia: Hi Sofia, platform eng, I'm looking after infra and SSO. Mainly worried about VPC and audit logs.

[00:00:38] Maya: Great. Quick agenda: show model catalog, how to pick open models, interpret the benchmark numbers, then Optimize suggestions for batching/quant and how routing & compatibility matrices work. Leave time for Qs and next steps.

[00:01:05] Luca: jumping in — opening the console, catalog view. You'll see models grouped by family, version and verified perf bullets. For open models we surface both CPU/GPU profiles and our validated latency numbers under typical short sequence loads.

[00:02:12] [screen share noise] Luca: see here we have 'Open-Llama-3-small' and 'Mistral-7b' entries, and each row has benchmark tabs: latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost-estimate. The compatibility matrix shows which quantizations and hardware kernels we validate — e.g., 4-bit quant on A10 has a different perf line than float16 on H100.

[00:03:04] Jordan: How do you calibrate those numbers? Our workload is 30-80 token prompts so micro-benchmarks matter.

[00:03:15] Luca: good Q — we run a synthetic workload that matches short prompt distributions and also run a small sample of customer prompts when provided. The numbers on the UI are the synthetic baselines; we recommend running a quick job with your prompt set — that's where Optimize helps by recommending batch sizes and kv cache config.

[00:04:02] Maya: also important is model quality vs cost tradeoff. For open models we show a small eval score (not perfect) and links to community evals. We don't assert that one model is best — we give the levers.

[00:04:20] Markus: Are these benchmarks single-tenant? If we go Dedicated will the numbers change?

[00:04:27] Priya: they can. Hosted numbers show multi-tenant averages with conservative queuing behavior. Dedicated tends to reduce p95 tails because of isolation — we add a note on the catalog rows about which numbers are from Dedicated runs versus shared.

[00:04:50] Sofia: VPC/Private question: can Redwood run in our VPC and still surface the same catalog and Optimize suggestions?

[00:04:58] Maya: yes — our Private deploys include the control plane endpoints that feed the Console. For air-gapped installs we can share an offline catalog and the Optimize tooling can run locally; you'll need our SE to help wire the telemetry to get accurate perf numbers.

[00:05:30] [00:05:30] Luca: demoing Optimize: you upload sample prompts (or paste) and Optimize simulates batching and caching. Example, with your short prompts Optimize suggests small batch sizes (4-8) and aggressive prefix cache for repeated context which reduces tokens/sec costs while keeping p95 low.

[00:06:12] Jordan: prefix cache… we're doing a lot of repeated system instructions; that could help. Does that change model outputs?

[00:06:20] Luca: it shouldn't change semantics — it's about reusing KV cache between requests with identical prefixes. We do warn about safety when prompts include ephemeral user data.

[00:06:48] Maya: switching back to catalog — here's the compatibility matrix we mentioned. It maps model architectures to tested kernel sets (e.g., flash-attn v3), supported quantizations, and known caveats. If you click 'view matrix' it shows kernel x hardware x quantization heatmap.

[00:07:20] Sofia: can we lock to specific kernels? We have compliance rules about deterministic outputs for audits.

[00:07:29] Luca: you can pin model variants and kernel sets in the deployment config — that makes rollouts reproducible. We also store model-version provenance in audit logs.

[00:08:05] Markus: what's the fallback policy if a GPU pool is saturated? We can't afford heavy SLA misses.

[00:08:12] Priya: routing policies let you fallback to a lower-cost or lower-latency variant — e.g., route to a smaller 7b model in another region or to a quantized variant. You set thresholds by latency/cost and Redwood will reroute automatically. We also support a synchronous fallback to a cached response when models are 2xx slow.

[00:09:00] Jordan: this is key. How do you test quality regression when fallback happens?

[00:09:06] Luca: we keep eval sets and track per-prompt regressions; you can tag critical prompts and get alerts if quality drops beyond a threshold. Optimize includes a small regression alert runner.

[00:09:32] [00:09:32] Maya: quick pause — any questions on the catalog UIs?

[00:09:40] Sofia: one more on security: KMS integration for keys at rest?

[00:09:45] Maya: yes, KMS + HSM options for Private and Dedicated, plus audit trails and SOC2 cert details are in the one-pager. We'll attach the compliance pack after the call.

[00:10:12] Luca: jumping to a concrete bench: I ran a short Mistral-7b quant test and Open-Llama baseline earlier. For 40-token requests on A10, Mistral p95 was ~180ms and Open-Llama ~240ms with 4-bit quant rounding. In Dedicated the p95 dropped ~20%. These are illustrative — yours may vary.

[00:11:05] Jordan: can you show me the raw CSV or spreadsheet for that?

[00:11:12] Luca: yes I'll include the spreadsheet link. It has columns: model, kernel, quant, hw, seq_len, p50, p95, tokens_per_sec, cost_est.

[00:11:30] [screen switch] Luca: here's Optimize's recommended config for a scenario: sequence 40, 50 RPS, low latency target. It suggests batch size 6, kv_cache true, prefer h100 kernel float16 for quality, fallback to quantized on A10 for cost.

[00:12:05] Markus: floats vs quant — do you support mixed precision or auto-switching?

[00:12:12] Priya: we support runtime variant switching with warm-up. Optimize can recommend a warm-up schedule; for deterministic audits you can lock to a single variant.

[00:12:40] Jordan: about endpoints — do you give a single API and you handle routing or do we have to modify clients?

[00:12:47] Maya: single API. You can pass routing hints in the call or let the platform decide based on policy. We also surface per-route dashboards for latency and cost.

[00:13:20] Sofia: any gotchas for on-prem? Our infra team worries about GPU drivers and kernel compilation.

[00:13:28] Luca: driver matrix is in the compatibility docs; our Private deployment engineers will coordinate driver versions and kernel builds. For air-gapped installs we provide an archive of validated kernels.

[00:14:02] [short pause] Jordan: timeline — we want to prove within 2–3 weeks that a 200ms p95 is achievable for our short prompts. Is that doable?

[00:14:12] Maya: yes, doable as a POC. Typical flow: you provide sample prompts and target SLAs, we run an initial perf pass on hosted or Dedicated baseline, then iterate. We'll propose a POC scope in the follow-up.

[00:14:35] Luca: I'll note: we prefer representative prompt sets with distribution of lengths and any few-shot context you use. That makes latency numbers realistic.

[00:15:00] [00:15:00] Jordan: ok good. Walk me through a real example of a compatibility mismatch — like a model that fails on a kernel?

[00:15:08] Luca: sure—there was a recent GLM-variant where flash-attn v2 produced a slightly higher memory footprint than expected on a5x, causing OOMs at sequence 1024. In the matrix we mark that kernel as 'untested' for seq>512 and recommend alternate kernel builds. That's why we surface caveats per-model.

[00:15:50] Sofia: that kind of transparency is helpful.

[00:16:00] [demo continues] Luca: flipping back to the Console's model detail page — you can click 'simulate workload' and get a predicted p95 curve vs RPS for selected hardware. Note the uncertainty band — those are empirical variance estimates.

[00:16:40] Jordan: accuracy metrics — you mentioned small eval. How should we trust those?

[00:16:46] Priya: they're heuristics — we surface multiple sources: internal eval runs, community benchmarks, and your private evals if you supply them. We prefer customers to run a small quality eval with their prompts.

[00:17:12] [00:17:12] Maya: tour wrap-up — we've covered catalog, compatibility, Optimize recommendations, and routing/fallback. Any final technical deep-dive requests?

[00:17:25] Jordan: I'd like an SE deep-dive on the perf harness and logs so our SREs can vet it. Also an itemized compliance checklist for Private deploy.

[00:17:36] Sofia: and sample deployment manifests for the kernel versions.

[00:17:42] Luca: noted. We'll prepare an SE deep-dive and attach the manifest snippets.

[00:17:50] [pause — small cross talk]

[00:18:05] Maya: ok next steps recap: Maya will send the benchmark sheet and recording; Luca will run a targeted perf pass once Jordan uploads prompts; we'll schedule POC kickoff tentative 2025-05-06.

[00:18:20] Jordan: sounds good. One operational question: billing for POC — do you provide credits or short-term discounted Dedicated?

[00:18:29] Maya: we usually offer trial credits and can provide a short-term discounted Dedicated window for POC. I'll loop in Channel/Finance as needed.

[00:18:45] Markus: any competitor differences you want to call out quickly?

[00:18:51] Maya: quick note — Anthropic and OpenAI are strong on model quality and ecosystem, but our differentiator here is inference routing + cost controls + unified dev experience across Private/Dedicated. Vertex is broader infra but less focused on per-token inference economics.

[00:19:20] [closing minutes — wrap and logistics] Maya: thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items. Luca any last notes?

[00:19:30] Luca: just one: please label the critical prompts for regression detection — makes alerting much easier.

[00:19:36] Jordan: will do.

[00:19:40] Maya: great — end of recording.
